extracted.intended_audience: researchers and administrative staff preparing NIH grant applications (senior/key personnel and biosketches)
extracted.subtask_short: NIH biosketch and key person profile
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form fields for completing Senior/Key Person Profiles and PHS 398-style biographical sketches for NIH grant applications, including required sections, page limits, education/training entries, publications, and research support listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — page limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Senior/key person must provide a biographical sketch following the specified format and must not exceed four pages per person. This instruction appears in all biographical sketch sections and applies to each individual listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — required top fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide NAME, POSITION TITLE, and eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These identifying fields must appear at the top of each biographical sketch exactly as shown in the sample format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training — required format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. List INSTITUTION AND LOCATION, DEGREE (if applicable), MM/YY, and FIELD OF STUDY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should be chronological starting from initial professional education and include institution/location, degree, date (MM/YY), and field. Examples in the biosketch show BS, DVM, PhD, Post-Doc, and research scientist positions with dates and fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise personal statement describing the individual's background, experience, and relevance to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should summarize scientific/leadership experience, specific technical expertise, past accomplishments relevant to the project, collaborations, and explain why the individual is well suited to execute or contribute to the proposed work. Examples include highlighting prior research on VLP vaccine development, leadership roles, and prior collaborations with other investigators named on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — B. Positions and Employment
rubrics_metrics.description: List positions and employment (with years) in chronological order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include institutional affiliations, roles/titles, and date ranges (years). The examples list research assistant, postdoctoral fellow, research scientist, principal scientist, faculty appointments, and industry leadership roles with start and end years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — Other Experience and Professional Memberships / Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: List other relevant experiences, professional memberships, honors, and notable service (e.g., study sections, review panels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include membership in societies, review panel service (NIH study sections), editorial or reviewer roles, travel awards, fellowships, and other honors that demonstrate professional standing and relevant contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — C. Selected Peer-reviewed Publications (Most relevant and Additional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a numbered list of selected peer-reviewed publications, separating 'Most relevant to current application' from 'Additional publications of importance to the field.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite full references (authors, title, journal, volume, pages, year). Use numbering and clearly label which items are most relevant to the current application. Include PMIDs or PMCID where useful (examples include both).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — D. Research Support (Ongoing and Completed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe ongoing and completed research support, listing grant numbers, PI/role, dates, funding agency, title, project goals, and the individual's role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ongoing support, provide current award identifier, PI name, dates, agency, project title, concise goals, and role (e.g., PI, Co-Investigator). For completed support, list prior grants with dates and roles. Examples show NIH R01/R21/R03/R44 entries with explicit goals and roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — Tailor personal statement to project relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal statements should explain how the individual's experience, technical expertise, and prior work position them to contribute to the specific aims of the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the personal statement to connect prior accomplishments (e.g., VLP vaccine development, CTL assays) and ongoing roles to how they will enable success of the proposed work. Mention specific collaborations and resources relevant to execution of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person Profile — required contact & affiliation fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile fields include Prefix, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Organization Name, Division, Position/Title, Department, Street1, Street2, Phone Number, Fax Number, E-Mail, Credential (e.g., agency login), Zip/Postal Code, Country, State, County/Parish, City.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all profile fields for each Senior/Key Person in the expanded Senior/Key Person Profile form to ensure accurate identification and contact information in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person Profile — project role and degree information
rubrics_metrics.description: For each Senior/Key Person provide Project Role, Other Project Role Category (if applicable), Degree Type, and Degree Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the role on the application (e.g., PI, Co-Investigator, Collaborator, Staff Scientist), categorize 'Other Project Role' when needed, and list degree type and year (e.g., PhD 2005).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments — biographical sketch and current & pending support
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach Biographical Sketch and Current & Pending Support documents to each Senior/Key Person profile as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms include buttons/fields to 'Attach Biographical Sketch' and 'Attach Current & Pending Support' with options to add, delete, and view attachments. Ensure attachments match the sample format and page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/form-filling guidance — handling many Senior/Key Persons
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure proper performance of the form after adding 20 additional Senior/Key Persons: save your application, close the Adobe Reader, and reopen it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a technical tip to avoid form performance issues when the expanded profile list grows large; follow these steps during form completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include patents and intellectual property in biosketch when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: List patents (title, filing/issued date, inventors) relevant to the individual's research contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents are appropriate material for the biographical sketch and should be listed (as shown in the example list of patent titles and filing dates) to demonstrate translational or IP-related accomplishments that support the proposed project's feasibility or investigator expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent citation and role labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: When listing publications, research support, and positions, use consistent formatting, full citation details, and explicitly state roles (e.g., PI, Co-Investigator, Subcontractor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency aids reviewers in quickly assessing relevance and contributions. Examples show standardized listing of grant numbers, PIs, dates, titles, goals, and roles.
